llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Mistral AI connector, but its setup instructions tell users to run unverified remote installer scripts directly in a shell.

dimensions.detail: Runtime tool scope is limited to Bash(oo *), which fits the connector purpose, but the connector can send user content through OOMOL/Mistral and act on Mistral account resources.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup includes curl-to-bash and PowerShell iex commands for an external installer without version pinning, checksum, signature verification, or a manual inspection step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger is broad for any Mistral AI request, but the artifact tags state-changing and destructive actions and instructs agents to confirm exact payloads and targets before running them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden persistence, memory writing, or privilege escalation is present in the artifact; setup may create a normal oo CLI login/session and OOMOL app connection when the user performs it.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose matches its capabilities: it uses the OOMOL oo CLI to operate Mistral AI and discloses read, write, upload, download, and destructive connector actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust OOMOL and are comfortable with Mistral account actions being mediated through the oo CLI. Avoid running the curl|bash or irm|iex installer commands as written; prefer a signed or version-pinned installer with checksum verification, and require explicit confirmation before any write or delete action.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: Installing the oo CLI is purpose-aligned, but the direct remote script execution is an accepted material supply-chain concern.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad Mistral AI routing is coherent with a connector skill and is partly mitigated by explicit confirmation instructions for write and destructive actions.
[T03] expected: The static finding is supported by artifact lines showing mutable remote installers piped directly to bash or PowerShell; there is no evidence of malicious payload, but the installation method warrants Review.
